reader.requirement: At --std 85 an alphanumeric argument position must take a data item of class alphabetic or alphanumeric (which in 1985 includes alphanumeric edited, numeric edited and every group item, §1985:IV.4.3.3) or a nonnumeric literal, refuse class numeric items, numeric literals and numeric expressions/functions, and use the argument's size.

edition-consulted.switches: sig.IntroducedIn > ctx.Edition.DialectLevel refuses a function not yet introduced (DiagnosticCatalog.IntrinsicFunctionNotYetIntroduced); the 1989 functions carry IntroducedIn 85 in IntrinsicCatalog, so --std 85 admits them
ArgPredicate.AppliesAt(ctx.Edition.Edition.Year) gates each per-position predicate by its Since year; the class screen itself (IntrinsicArgumentRules.Violation over Verified) is edition-blind
ConstructRegistry NumericFunctionIdentifierOperand2002: at --std 85 a numeric/integer function is admitted only inside an arithmetic expression (a nested function argument is one)

reader.edition-search: grep -n 'Edition|CobolVersion|since|Std|1985|1989' over IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs and IntrinsicBinder.cs; the only edition reads on the argument path are ArgPredicate.Since/AppliesAt, sig.IntroducedIn and the 2002 placement construct; ClassOf1/ClassOfPlace/ClassOfItem/ClassOfPic/Admissible/Violation consult no edition
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: ClassStringRules (ByClass over TableTwoClass) admits numeric-edited and groups as class alphanumeric at every edition, which is the 1985 class definition; national members unreachable at 85
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f33_01 covers PIC A, PIC X, a group and a literal; numeric-edited, alphanumeric-edited, ref-mod at its bounds, an ODO group, ALL subscripts and the refusal half are not exercised

probes.expected: alphabetic and alphanumeric-class items (incl. numeric edited, alphanumeric edited, groups, ref-mod views, ODO groups at current size) and nonnumeric literals admitted, their size used

probes.printed: COBOL1627 on REVERSE(PIC 9(3)), REVERSE(123), UPPER-CASE(BINARY item), LOWER-CASE(NU + 1), REVERSE(FUNCTION LOG (2)); exit 65
probes.expected: refused: a numeric item, numeric literal, expression or numeric function is not class alphabetic/alphanumeric nor a nonnumeric literal

probes.expected: a later edition's operand forms (national literal, floating-point literal) are not 1985 literals and are refused

reader.notes: ORD's 2002-only CharacterCategory predicate (Since 2002) is the one place the 85 arm of this class reading is switched; REVERSE/UPPER-CASE/LOWER-CASE carry only MinWidth(1) with Since 85. An ODO group argument is read at its current size (REVERSE gave 3 characters at N=2).

refuter.evidence: Attacked the figurative-constant form the reader did not try: afig-001 at --std 85 admits UPPER-CASE(SPACE)=[ ], LENGTH(SPACE)=1, REVERSE(ALL "AB")=[BA] (same at --std 2023, afig-002). AR3 asks for 'a nonnumeric literal'; §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR1 makes argument-1 'an identifier, a literal, or an arithmetic expression', and §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3 (a subsection of 4.2.2.2 Literals) lets a figurative constant stand 'whenever literal appears in a format' with the one exception that a numeric-literal position takes only ZERO; the compiler matches that reading exactly (SPACE/HIGH-VALUE/QUOTE/ALL refused in numeric positions, admitted in alphanumeric ones), and ALL literal's length is the literal's (4.2.2.2.3). Refusal half: aref2-001 refuses REVERSE(IXD USAGE INDEX) COBOL6979, UPPER-CASE(IX) COBOL1637, REVERSE(FUNCTION LOG (5)) and LOWER-CASE(FUNCTION INTEGER (5)) COBOL1627, REVERSE(X"41") COBOL0900 (hex literal is not a 1985 nonnumeric literal). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.2 AR3 the text is in AR3; OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR1 the text is in SR1; OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3 the text is in the clause.
